{{2025–26 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2025–26 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wildcats, founding members of the [[Southeastern Conference]], played their home games at [[Rupp Arena]] and were led by [[Mark Pope]] in his second season as head coach for the Wildcats. 

==Previous season==
The [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] with a record of {{Win-loss record|w=24|l=12}}, {{Win-loss record|w=10|l=8}} in SEC play to finish in a 3-way tie for seventh place in the SEC. The Wildcats earned a number six seed in the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they won the second-round game against [[2024–25 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]] then lost to [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where the Wildcats made it to the Sweet 16 by defeating [[2024–25 Troy Trojans men's basketball team|Troy]], 76–57, in the first round and [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]], 84–75, in the second round.  The Wildcats lost to rival [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 78–65, in the Sweet Sixteen, finishing the season with an overall record of 24–12.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Ben|title=Kentucky's basketball season ends with lopsided NCAA Tournament loss to rival Tennessee |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article303006499.html |website=kentucky.com |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |access-date=June 7, 2025 |date=March 29, 2025}}</ref>

==Offseason==
===Departures===
Kentucky had 5 departures from the 2025 team that were lost to exhausted eligibility.  On March 31 Kerr Kriisa announced his entry into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Ben |title=Kerr Kriisa is the first UK basketball player to make a move. He's in the transfer portal |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article303158816.html |website=kentucky.com |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |access-date=March 31, 2025 |date=March 31, 2025}}</ref>  On April 8 Kriisa committed to play for [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Drummond |first1=Cameron |title=After one season with Kentucky, Kerr Kriisa has found a new school to play for |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article303239741.html |website=kentucky.com |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |access-date=April 8, 2025 |date=April 8, 2025}}</ref> On April 22 Travis Perry put his name in the transfer portal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=Kentucky basketball's Travis Perry, in-state star, puts name into NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/04/22/travis-perry-kentucky-basketball-freshman-ncaa-transfer-portal/82720037007/ |website=courier-journal.com |publisher=Courier-Journal |access-date=April 22, 2025 |date=April 22, 2025}}</ref> On May 4 Perry committed to play for SEC rival [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=Kentucky basketball's Travis Perry, in-state star, puts name into NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2025/05/04/travis-perry-ole-miss-basketball-transfer-kentucky/83446748007/ |website=clarionledger.com |publisher=Clarion Ledger |access-date=May 4, 2025 |date=May 4, 2025}}</ref>

===Incoming transfers===
Prior to the end of the 2025 season Kentucky received its first transfer commitment for the next season from forward Kam Williams, who transferred from [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]], on March 29.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Drummond |first1=Cameron |title=Three takeaways from Kentucky basketball's loss to Oakland in the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article303004314.html |website=kentucky.com |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |access-date=March 29, 2025 |date=March 29, 2025}}</ref> On April 5 guard Jaland Lowe, transferring from [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], committed to play for Kentucky.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=Jaland Lowe commits to Kentucky basketball: What to know about transfer portal addition |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/04/05/jaland-lowe-kentucky-basketball-roster-2025-26-mark-pope-recruiting-transfer-portal/82719880007/ |website=courier-journal.com |publisher=Courier-Journal |access-date=April 5, 2025 |date=April 5, 2025}}</ref> Two days later on April 7 former [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] forward Mouhamed Dioubate became the third transfer commitment.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=Mouhamed Dioubate picks Kentucky basketball: What to know about transfer portal addition |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/04/07/kentucky-basketball-transfer-portal-mouhamed-diabate-uk-roster-mark-pope-recruiting/82719904007/ |website=courier-journal.com |publisher=Courier-Journal |access-date=April 7, 2025 |date=April 7, 2025}}</ref> One day later, one of the top forwards in the portal, former [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] forward [[Jayden Quaintance]] committed. Quaintance was previously a signee with Kentucky in the 2024 class, but decommitted once former coach [[John Calipari]] became the [[Arkansas Razorbacks|Arkansas]] head coach.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/espngamer/ncb/story/_/id/44586018/ex-arizona-state-star-jayden-quaintance-re-commits-kentucky |title=Ex-Arizona State star Jayden Quaintance recommits to Kentucky|first=Jonathan |last=Givony |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=April 8, 2025 |access-date=April 8, 2025}}</ref> On April 21 former [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] guard Denzel Aberdeen committed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=
Denzel Aberdeen commits to Kentucky basketball: What to know about transfer portal guard |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/04/21/denzel-aberdeen-kentucky-basketball-roster-2025-26-mark-pope-recruiting-transfer-portal/82719887007/ |website=courier-journal.com |publisher=Courier-Journal |access-date=April 21, 2025 |date=April 21, 2025}}</ref>  The last member of the transfer class is center Reece Potter, who committed on May 5 after transferring from [[Miami RedHawks men's basketball|Miami (OH)]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=
Reece Potter commits to Kentucky basketball: What to know about transfer portal addition |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/05/05/reece-potter-kentucky-basketball-roster-2025-26-mark-pope-recruiting-transfer-portal/82719899007/ |website=courier-journal.com |publisher=Courier-Journal |access-date=May 5, 2025 |date=May 5, 2025}}</ref> This years team, had a high [[Name, image and likeness|NIL]] (Name Image and Likeness) value, of around $22M.
